topic: How does defocused reflector gain loss impact link budget margins for SNR compared to conventional designs?
consensus_response: Defocused reflector gain loss reduces antenna gain, broadens beam patterns, and increases spill-over loss, degrading SNR and system capacity. This impacts link budget margins, affecting network reliability and QoS provisioning. Robust beamforming techniques can mitigate this by optimizing SNR and minimizing interference.
reference_context: Defocused reflectors suffer 1.52-6 dB gain loss, with spill-over loss ranging from 4.95-5.655 dB, impacting system performance.
